why: Index order does not matter and values are distinct, so this is 3-sum-smaller on the sorted array: count triples of values with sum <= t. Fix the smallest value, then two pointers over the rest count all pairs fitting the remaining budget.
hints: Since the triple is ordered by value, not position, you are free to sort. What does the problem become on a sorted array?
Fix i as the smallest value; you need pairs lo < hi in the suffix with a[lo] + a[hi] <= t - a[i]. If a[lo] + a[hi] fits, every hi' in (lo, hi] also fits with lo.

Sort; for each i, set lo = i+1, hi = n-1; when the pair fits add hi - lo and move lo up, otherwise move hi down. O(n^2) worst case, fine for n = 10^4, with early break when even the two smallest exceed the budget.
pitfalls: t and the sums can exceed 2^31 - 1; use 64-bit types outside Python.
Do not impose a < b < c on the original indices.
Count is up to C(10^4, 3), about 1.7 * 10^11, so it needs a 64-bit integer too.
